tells.1: Stacked three-part lists ('put the kettle on, catch your breath and enjoy…', 'talk through…, brush up…, catch up…') with the warmer framing smoothed into neutral phrasing
tells.2: Over-tidied structure: the welcome is moved to the top, the fondant line stands alone, and it ends on a clipped one-line sign-off, which reads a bit sterile
tells.3: Choppy one-idea paragraphs and a mismatched closer ('Wherever you are with your winter preparations, we'd love to hear how your season went') created by mechanical restructuring
tells.4: The em dash in the closing line, plus the familiar three-item lists, though both are common in human writing
tells.5: Redundant restatement ('you're not alone. Most of us are in the same boat') and terse fragments ('£35 a head. Bring your questions…') that feel deliberately casual

reason: Version 4 has the most natural, distinctive voice ('Well…certainly kept us on our toes', 'It's been a tough one'), and its closing welcome works as a lead-in to the report. The other versions read like edits that either flatten that voice or rearrange it awkwardly.
